Subject: Regulus DPA — incident notification, scope & cooperation

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Regulus' DPA review, Legal has flagged the incident notification section. A few specific asks from our side:

- Initial notification timeline for confirmed incidents (we typically ask for 48–72 hours).
- Required contents of the notice (scope, affected data classes, mitigating steps, point of contact).
- Evidence and cooperation: we need a clear commitment to preserve/export logs and provide forensic support for 30 days after an incident, plus a handover process for regulators.
- Subprocessor involvement: if a subprocessor is root cause, we need confirmation that Redwood will coordinate notices and provide subprocessor contact info.

I've attached the Regulus DPA redline with proposed language (Regulus_DPA_Incident_Requests.docx) and a short questionnaire. Can you confirm Redwood's standard position and whether you can accept the 48-hour initial notice for confirmed incidents?

Appreciate it — Samantha

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Legal and Security so we can align on specific clause language. High level notes from product/ops:

- Redwood's baseline: we notify customers "without undue delay" and provide an initial assessment typically within 48 hours for confirmed incidents that materially impact customer data. We prefer to keep "without undue delay" in contract language but accept a commitment to an initial update within 48 hours for confirmed incidents if that helps Regulus.
- We can commit to: initial notification (48 hours for confirmed incidents), regular updates (every 48–72 hours) until remediation, and a formal post-incident report within 14 calendar days.
- Evidence handover: we will provide logs, timelines, and diagnostic exports where legally and technically permissible. For forensic artifacts involving third-party subprocessors we will coordinate requests and work to obtain relevant records.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a public subprocessor list and will notify affected customers when a subprocessor is implicated.

Attaching our incident-notice template for reference. Laura/Vivek/Neha — can you comment on tightening language (time-to-initial-notice, definition of "security incident", and evidence preservation windows)?

Priyom —

Quick legal take (redlines below are high level; I'll produce markups after the thread):

- Definition: we need to narrow "security incident" so it covers unauthorized access, exfiltration, destruction, or modification of Regulus data (and exclude routine operational issues). That avoids ambiguity on what triggers the 48-hour clock.
- Initial notification: Regulus has asked for 48–72 hours. Security is comfortable committing to initial notice for "confirmed" incidents in 48 hours; for suspected incidents we should commit to notifying "without undue delay" and escalate to confirmed/not-confirmed status within 72 hours if investigation permits.
- Evidence preservation: propose explicit 90-day preservation for forensic artifacts (logs, images) unless legal hold or export controls prevent us. We can offer a 30-day export window with options to extend upon reasonable request citing legal/regulatory need.
- Subprocessors: include an obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain subprocessor artifacts and a requirement to provide contact details for the implicated subprocessor. We should keep carveouts for situations where contractually blocked.
- Regulatory handover: commit to reasonable assistance for customer regulatory inquiries and to provide a full timeline and remediation plan in the post-incident report.

I don't object to the 48-hour initial notice for confirmed incidents so long as definition/confirmation language is tightened and we include the investigatory window and carveouts.

Laura

Adding a couple operational constraints from Security:

- Data export windows: for any export of logs or VM images we need a secure transfer channel (SFTP with MFA or an encrypted Drive share) and an agreed TTL for the exported artifacts. 30 days default seems workable, but we need an extension process.
- Preservation vs. export: preserving artifacts in our environment for 90 days is feasible; exporting may be restricted by third-party terms (e.g., cloud provider snapshot restrictions). We should call out exceptions and a timeline to communicate them to the customer.
- Forensic support: we can provide a named contact and up to 10 hours of investigative support included; additional hours can be billed or handled under a premium support engagement. (Regulus may want more — flag for procurement/contract).

Vivek

Subject: Re: Regulus DPA — incident notification, scope & cooperation

Samantha —

Thanks for patience while we reviewed internally. Proposed compromise to include in the DPA (summary, contract-ready language to follow):

1) Definition: "Security Incident" means an event resulting in unauthorized access to, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of Regulus Health data processed by Redwood.

2) Initial notification: Redwood will provide Customers with an initial notification for confirmed Security Incidents affecting Customer data within 48 hours of confirmation. For suspected incidents, Redwood will notify without undue delay and provide confirmation or rejection within 72 hours if feasible.

3) Updates & post-incident report: Redwood will provide progress updates every 48–72 hours and deliver a post-incident report (root cause, scope, remedial actions) within 14 days of confirmation. Where regulatory needs require more detail, Redwood will cooperate to extend reporting timelines.

4) Evidence & preservation: Redwood will preserve forensic artifacts for 90 days by default and will export logs/artifacts within 30 days upon request where technically and contractually allowed. Export will use a secure transfer mechanism and include a named Redwood contact. Extensions can be requested and will be granted on a reasonable basis.

5) Subprocessors: If a Redwood subprocessor is implicated, Redwood will: (a) inform the affected customer promptly; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain subprocessor artifacts; and (c) provide subprocessor contact information unless prohibited by the subprocessor agreement.

6) Forensic assistance: Redwood will provide up to 10 hours of included investigative assistance; additional support will be available under a professional services agreement.

If this package looks acceptable, Laura will prepare redline language that meets Regulus' needs and our operational constraints. Happy to hop on a short call to resolve any remaining tradeoffs.

Best,
Priyom

--

Priyom / Laura / Vivek —

Appreciate the thoughtful response and internal coordination. Regulus is generally comfortable with the compromise: initial notification within 48 hours for confirmed incidents, 14-day post-incident report, and the proposed subprocessor coordination language. A few follow-ups before Legal signs off:

- Can Redwood confirm the process for extending the 30-day export window (what is "reasonable" and how fast will extensions be granted)?
- Please add explicit language that Redwood will preserve artifacts for at least 90 days unless doing so would violate law or an overriding third-party term; in such a case Redwood must notify Regulus and propose alternative evidence access.
- Regulus would like confirmation that included 10 hours of forensic support can be used for regulator-facing preparation (e.g., draft timeline, help with regulator Qs) and that additional hours are available on a time-and-materials basis.

If you can provide a redline that incorporates the small clarifications above, we can proceed to signature. Also please share SOC 2 Type II access or an equivalent attestation as supporting evidence.

I'll await Laura's redline and Vivek's short note about export extension timing.

Thanks,
Samantha
